title: Multimodal Deep Learning
byline: Akkus, Chu, Dani, Ebert et al. (LMU Munich seminar booklet) · arXiv 2301.04856, January 2023
note: A student-written seminar booklet, each section by different authors; its state of the art is early 2023. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A survey of deep learning that combines text and images, written by students in an LMU Munich seminar. It first reviews the state of the art separately in NLP (word embeddings to transformers and large language models) and computer vision (CNNs to vision transformers and self-supervised learning), with the datasets and benchmarks for each. The main part covers multimodal architectures in both directions: image captioning, text-to-image generation (DALL-E, diffusion models), images grounding language models, text supervising vision models (CLIP), and joint models of both modalities. Further chapters extend to audio and video, mixing structured data with text and images, multipurpose models like Gato and Perceiver, and generative art.
